topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Traditional Therapies: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities—including surgery, radiation, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance via efflux pumps.

topics.label: Targeting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities and DNA Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how therapeutic strategies exploit intrinsic cellular weaknesses, such as hormone dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint losses, oncolytic viral sensitivity, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene Targeting and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address therapies targeting oncogenic driver mutations, focusing on kinase inhibitor mechanisms, structural selectivity, and mechanisms of resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Cancer Therapeutics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms and applications of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor-associated surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer Immunosurveillance and Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the immune system's relationship with cancer and detail immunotherapeutic strategies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, neoantigen targeting, BiTEs, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Therapeutic Challenges, Progress, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of cancer therapy, reflecting on epidemiological trends, genomic stratification, ongoing clinical challenges, and future prospects.
